item.title: S. Korea's foreign ministry expresses regret to Russia over warplanes' KADIZ entry
item.author: The Korea Herald
item.description: The foreign ministry said Tuesday it has conveyed its regret to Russia over the entry of Russian military aircraft into the country's air defense zone and called for measures to prevent a recurrence. About five Russian military aircraft entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone over the East Sea earlier in the day and approached the edge of South Korea's territorial airspace near Ulleung Island, according to the Joint Chiefs of Staff. item.title: Middle schooler identified as suspect behind fake bomb threat at department store
item.author: The Korea Herald
item.description: A middle school student has been identified as the suspect behind a fax message claiming an explosive was planted at a store of Shinsegae, a major department store chain, sources said Tuesday. The message was sent to police Sunday evening, prompting a search of all 13 Shinsegae branches across the nation, as the note had not specified a branch. No explosives were found. item.title: BTS back in military uniform? Here's what happened
item.author: The Korea Herald
item.description: BTS’ V has gone viral after fellow servicemen praised his performance during his first reserve forces training in November, where he reportedly finished first in a mock battle. Jin, Jimin and J-Hope also completed their reserve forces training together during the group’s ongoing Arirang World Tour.

item.title: Evan to embark on tour across Asia, North America in 2027
item.author: The Korea Herald
item.description: K-pop singer Evan, formerly of Enhypen, will begin a tour to meet fans in January, visiting 14 cities across Asia and North America, Belift Lab announced Tuesday. Titled "Everlasting," the tour will begin in Tokyo and Incheon in January, followed by stops in Bangkok, Hong Kong and Taipei, Taiwan, in February. item.title: LG Chem backs smaller partners with price cuts and loans
item.author: The Korea Herald
item.description: LG Chem is supporting small and midsize suppliers and customers through price relief, low-interest financing, technical assistance and workforce training to help them cut costs and improve their competitiveness. To ease the impact on production costs of fluctuating oil prices, LG Chem is temporarily lowering prices on some of the petrochemical products it sells to smaller client companies that make vinyl products and packaging materials.
